target_customer: Mid to large companies whose HR and finance teams run org design and headcount planning
problem: Org design and workforce planning ran in spreadsheets, making restructuring and headcount scenarios slow and error prone.
product_category: Org design and strategic workforce planning software

founders.name: Dave Y. Kim
founders.background_notes: Founding engineer at kiwi.ai; head of mobile then integration lead at Sentiance per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Scenario modeling and org charts on HRIS data are standard SaaS engineering; integrations with HR systems were the main work.

defensibility.rationale: Planning data and workflows create some lock in, but incumbents such as Orgvue and ChartHop already offered similar tools and HR suites could rebuild it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Dayforce acquired Agentnoon and launched its Strategic Workforce Planning product on it, announced 2025-10-07, so an HR suite vendor absorbed the wedge.

market_need_then: Companies were reshaping organizations through 2022 hiring swings and later layoffs, and planning was still done in spreadsheets; sources opened give no direct demand data, so this is inferred from the product category only.

branding.domain_note: agentnoon.com now redirects to Dayforce (301) after the acquisition.

rebrands.why: Product re-platformed inside Dayforce after acquisition per Dayforce release.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand press found; the name has no stated origin and was retired into the acquirer's product name.

outcome_analysis: Agentnoon stayed small, with an aggregator total near 500K, then was acquired by Dayforce, announced on 2025-10-07 alongside Dayforce's Strategic Workforce Planning launch. The deal gave an HR suite vendor a fast route to a product, so the outcome looks like a technology and team acquisition at undisclosed terms rather than a venture scale exit; the success code other reflects an acquisition with unknown price.
notes: Directory status says Active but the domain redirects to Dayforce and Dayforce and Osler confirm an acquisition announced 2025-10-07; treat as acquired. Funding unverified: Welcome to the Jungle lists a 0.2M seed in 2022-08, CB Insights lists about 500K over six rounds, Bouncewatch lists a pre seed with 3 Davidovs Venture Collective in 2022-03; sources conflict so no rounds recorded. Investor names seen only in aggregators (Y Combinator, Liquid 2 Ventures, Tribe Capital, Google for Startups Accelerator Canada). Acquisition price not disclosed. No dated competitor sources near the batch found; search results were current comparison pages. Name origin and logo not found.
